items.item: `Sources/Memory Mapping/Memory.Allocation.Histogram.swift`: when the values span fewer than `buckets -
items.reason: Bucket count clamped to min(buckets, span); tests for a single value, a narrow span and a wide span.

Removed the unused sampleInterval parameter (interval sampling would need a background thread, and Linux statistics are thread-scoped so another thread would read the wrong counters). track now samples once after the operation, so the peak is never zero for an operation that allocates; doc comment says so.

Net bytes cannot be computed: Statistics carries no freed-bytes figure (Linux interposer tracks bytes_allocated only). Removed Net.bytes; the gross figure stays available as detector.delta().bytes.allocated, and Leak.Error's description now says 'Bytes allocated since baseline' instead of 'Net bytes'. No test: this is an API removal, and leak counts are not deterministic enough to assert.

items.item: Compose the Windows file-lock owner, acquire and retain the requested lock for the mapping lifetime
items.reason: Memory.Lock.Token.acquire is no longer #if !os(Windows) (every Kernel name it uses exists on Windows: Descriptor.Duplicate, Lock.lock/unlock, Close). Windows Memory.Map.open(fileHandle:) now acquires the coordinated lock after mapping, unmaps and throws .fileLock on failure, and stores the token, which unmap() releases once. Windows-only integration test pins that another handle's Immediate exclusive lock fails while mapped and succeeds after unmap. Not compiled here: Windows only, needs ci.yml.

api_changes: Windows: Memory.Map.open(fileHandle:...) with default or coordinated safety now takes a blocking LockFileEx lock (behaviour change: a second exclusive coordinated mapping of the same file blocks, also within one process since Windows locks are per handle)
notes: No uses of track(sampleInterval:), net.bytes or Windows Memory.Map.open(fileHandle:) found outside swift-memory-mapping. Linux build compiles Memory.Lock.Token.swift unchanged except indentation.
